:::{#exm-moore-penrose-eigendecomposition}
#### The Moore-Penrose inverse of a rank-one symmetric matrix

For the [symmetric matrix](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix) $\matr{S} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
an [eigendecomposition](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-eigendecomposition) is

$$
\matr{S}
= \underbrace{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}}_{\matr{Q}}
  \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}}_{\matr{\Eigvals}}
  \tp{\matr{Q}}.
$$

Inverting only the nonzero [eigenvalue](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-eigenvalue) gives $\matr{\Eigvals}^+ = \begin{bmatrix} 1/2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, so

$$
\ba
\matr{S}^+
&= \matr{Q}\matr{\Eigvals}^+\tp{\matr{Q}}
&& \text{(@thm-moore-penrose-eigendecomposition)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(only the first column of } \matr{Q} \text{ contributes)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}.
\ea
$$

Condition 1 of @def-moore-penrose holds:
$\matr{S}\matr{S}^+ = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
and multiplying by $\matr{S}$ again gives $\matr{S}$.
An [inverse](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-inverse) of $\matr{S}$ itself does not exist, because $\matr{S}$ has a zero eigenvalue.

:::
